answer: Daily split commitment names this mechanism: each identity must post a unique context-bound delta to its terrace ledger every block. The enforcement rule freezes any two identities for one full epoch when their posted deltas overlap above a fixed threshold. The concrete cost each attacker identity pays is a walnut-sized compute pledge, spent daily on a fresh local task. Because clones share one state, they cannot produce divergent local outputs, so the threshold always catches them.
